sources.note: Replaces the monotonic zoom-in that tool-using video agents follow once they pick a region with a policy that self-checks each tool observation and can switch regions, and trains it with turn-level credit applied multiplicatively -- reweighting the trajectory advantage's magnitude while preserving its sign -- rather than additively.
sources.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

sources.note: Injects a retrieved solved problem, with its full worked solution, into the middle of a reasoning model's own thinking trace at each step boundary, using the model's current intermediate answer as the retrieval query.
sources.title: ThinkRetrieve: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Traces for Test-Time Scaling

sources.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
sources.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

result.definition: An early mistake propagating through a long trajectory because nothing revisits it, and across 3 sources the failure that motivates the archive's recovery mechanisms. Its instances: agents following a monotonic zoom-in once a region is chosen, so an early wrong commitment propagates irreversibly; retrieval fixed before reasoning begins, so a wrong initial context is never corrected; and a search agent without reversible actions unable to discard a state it has diagnosed as unreliable. The remedies in the corpus are self-checking with region switching, retrieval interleaved through the trace, and explicit reflect and backtrack actions -- whose ablation finds diagnosis and recovery separately necessary. The archive's related caution is that the recovery mechanism must be selective: raising the rate at which a model announces a correction is anti-correlated with accuracy.
